facts.value: The major factors affecting how a business is organized include the size and scope of the business, sector and country, tax advantages, disclosure and compliance requirements, and control and coordination requirements.
facts.programme_association: Business Communication Degree Concentration | ASU Online

facts.value: Smaller businesses are more flexible, while larger businesses tend to be organized as corporations or partnerships.
facts.programme_association: Business Communication Degree Concentration | ASU Online

facts.value: A business that wishes to raise money on a stock market or be owned by a wide range of people will often need to adopt a specific legal form.
facts.programme_association: Business Communication Degree Concentration | ASU Online

facts.value: Most businesses operate through a separate entity such as a corporation or a partnership, which may be organized by filing charter documents and complying with ongoing obligations.
facts.programme_association: Business Communication Degree Concentration | ASU Online

facts.value: Shareholders in a corporation, limited partners in a limited partnership, and members in a limited liability company are typically shielded from personal liability for the entity's debts.
facts.programme_association: Business Communication Degree Concentration | ASU Online

facts.value: The terms of a partnership are partly governed by a partnership agreement and partly by the law of the jurisdiction where the partnership is located.
facts.programme_association: Business Communication Degree Concentration | ASU Online

facts.value: A single person who owns and runs a business is known as a sole proprietor, regardless of whether the ownership is direct or through a formally organized entity.
facts.programme_association: Business Communication Degree Concentration | ASU Online

facts.value: Corporations may face double taxation, where profits are taxed at the corporate level and again at the individual level when dividends are distributed.
facts.programme_association: Business Communication Degree Concentration | ASU Online

facts.value: Laws may treat small corporations differently from large ones, allowing exemptions from certain legal filing requirements or labor laws.
facts.programme_association: Business Communication Degree Concentration | ASU Online

facts.value: Going public through an initial public offering (IPO) means that part of the business will be owned by the public and requires tighter disclosure and compliance with laws.
facts.programme_association: Business Communication Degree Concentration | ASU Online
